newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Swiss judge in Sri Lanka to pursue paedophile case.
newsitem.headline: Swiss judge in Sri Lanka to pursue paedophile case.

text.p: A Swiss judge and two police officers arrived in Sri Lanka on Wednesday to investigate local connections of a suspected Swiss paedophile arrested in Bern recently, a senior police officer said.

The Swiss officials were in the island to collect evidence that would be used in the suspect's prosecution in Switzerland, Mohammed Nizam, deputy inspector general of the police crimes branch, told Reuters.
Nizam declined to identify the suspect.
"There had been a young Sri Lankan boy with him when he was arrested," Nizam said. "It is suspected he took more Sri Lankan boys to that country."
Sri Lanka has been cooperating with authorities abroad in a bid to clamp down on child abusers operating in the country, widely believed to be a popular destination for foreign paedophiles.
In January, Dutch police officals paid a similar visit to Sri Lanka on the trail of at least eight young boys who were allegedly abused by a Dutch investor.
"This sort of cooperation is very encouraging. It sends a strong message to the world's paedophiles," Nizam said.
Earlier this month, Swiss authorities remanded a suspected Swiss child abuser after he was deported by Sri Lanka.
They said a Zurich court would try 54-year-old Viktor Baumann for alleged child abuse in Sri Lanka.
Sexual abuse carries a maximum penalty of five years in prison in Switzerland.
A Sri Lankan court in January sentenced another Swiss, Armin Pfaffhauser, to two years in prison for having sex with boys.
Sri Lanka passed tough new laws in 1995 aimed at discouraging foreign tourists seeking sex with children and put police on alert for paedophiles.

The law calls for a minimum 10 years' jail-term and a maximum 20-year sentence for pimps and their clients. It pushed minimum age of consent up to 18 for boys and 16 for girls, making sex with anyone under this age a crime.
